title: My peace I give (John 14:27)
hook: not as the world gives; said at every Mass before the sign of peace

segments.voice: Yesterday, many mansions: a place prepared for frightened friends. Your line was a place for you.

Partway through Mass, a little after the Our Father, strangers turn to each other. A handshake across the pew. A nod to the teenager behind, a hug for a mother, a wave to someone too far away to reach. Peace be with you. Just before that moment, the priest says a short prayer that recalls a single sentence Jesus spoke at the Last Supper. It goes by quickly. Here's where it started.
screen: `STRANGERS TURN TO EACH OTHER.` → `PEACE BE WITH YOU.` → `A SENTENCE FROM THE SUPPER.`

segments.voice: Jesus is still at the table, telling his friends he's leaving. He's promised them the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, who will teach them and remind them of everything. Then, like someone at a doorway saying goodbye, he leaves them a gift. In the Douay-Rheims: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, do I give unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid." Peace, shalom, was an everyday word of greeting; after Easter Jesus will greet these same friends with it: peace be to you. Here he takes that everyday word and fills it. My peace. Not as the world gives. The world usually gives peace as an absence: no war, no noise, no problems, everything finally sorted out. Peace when the to-do list is done. Jesus says this to men who are about to watch him arrested, who will scatter in fear and hide behind locked doors. Nothing around them will be calm. Whatever his peace is, it isn't the absence of trouble. It's given in the middle of it. Perhaps that's why the Church puts it where it does. Before the sign of peace, the priest addresses Christ, recalling that he said to the apostles, peace I leave you, my peace I give you, and asks him to look not on our sins but on the faith of his Church. Then the peace is passed, hand to hand. Not a feeling people work up, but a gift handed on.
screen: `A GOODBYE GIFT AT THE DOOR.` · `SHALOM, FILLED.` · `PEACE IN THE MIDDLE OF TROUBLE.` · `THE PRAYER BEFORE THE SIGN OF PEACE.` · then, large: `MY PEACE I GIVE.`

segments.voice: Notice whatever is unsettled today, and don't try to fix it; breathe in as if you were being handed something, and out as if you were setting it down. Then think of one person you're tense with, or haven't spoken to in a while, and picture turning to them, as at Mass, and offering your hand. If you pray, hold the line, my peace I give unto you; if you don't, just hold the picture.
Eirene. The Greek word for peace, standing for shalom: Jesus's farewell gift at the supper, not as the world gives it. Today's word.
Your line: not as the world gives. Peace comes before things are sorted out, not after. Day five hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: At Mass, after the Our Father, the priest prays a prayer recalling John 14:27 and says, "The peace of the Lord be with you always"; then people may exchange a sign of peace with those near them.

fork.setup: you're saying goodbye to friends who will soon be frightened and scattered. what do you leave them?
options: your peace, not as the world gives.
a promise that nothing bad will happen.

original.note: Greek: peace (John 14:27), standing for the Hebrew shalom.

trapdoor: what you thought: peace means quiet and calm.
what it means: a peace given in the middle of trouble, as a farewell gift, not earned by fixing everything.
what a scholar hears: eirēnē is the Greek Bible's word for shalom, an everyday greeting; the Roman Missal's prayer before the sign of peace quotes John 14:27.
guess: peace, given even in the middle of trouble
a calm that comes once all trouble is gone
a formal greeting said only by priests

chat.says: Why do people shake hands and say peace be with you partway through Mass?
options: It's the sign of peace, recalling Jesus at the supper: my peace I give, not as the world gives.
It's a welcome for newcomers, so strangers in the pew can introduce themselves.
It marks the moment the Mass is over and people are free to head home.
chat.meaning: Before the sign of peace, the priest recalls Jesus's words at the Last Supper. The peace is a gift handed on, not a feeling worked up.

Paraclete.meaning: a name for the Holy Spirit, who Jesus says will teach them

shalom.meaning: Hebrew: peace, an everyday word of greeting

Our Father.meaning: the Lord's Prayer, the prayer Jesus taught

Last Supper.meaning: Jesus's final meal with his friends, the night before he died

Douay-Rheims.meaning: the old Catholic English translation of the Bible

notes: The Missal prayer before the sign of peace is paraphrased, not quoted (current English translation is under copyright).
The sign of peace is optional ('may'); hook says 'every Sunday' for the moment. Keeper may prefer 'most Sundays'.
Eirēnē as the Greek rendering of shalom. Confirm.
The index hook says 'said at every Mass'; the prayer before the sign of peace is part of every Mass in the Ordinary Form. Confirm.
